methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $640M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $6.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Solugen, a Series D climate and energy technology company founded by Gaurab Chakrabarti and Sean Hunt, has raised $640M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (Lilium, LNZA) and eight private—spanning climate and energy infrastructure, including stage-adjacent companies such as Redwood Materials (Series E, $6.0B), KoBold Metals (Series C, $3.0B), Electric Hydrogen (Series C, $1.0B), and Amogy (Series C, $700M).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, implies a valuation of $960M. Peer-median analysis across the four most comparable companies yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $6.0B, reflecting variability in technology maturity and commercial readiness within the cohort.

Synthesizing both methods produces a valuation range of $816M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.5B. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects material uncertainty around whether Solugen's market position and technology risk profile align more closely with earlier-stage peers or with more mature entrants. Key sensitivities include capital efficiency relative to peers, path to commercialization, and subsidy regime durability.
